gap: No result ChatGPT got states what a NAS costs against iCloud+ 2 TB ($9.99 a month, $119.88 a year). Before drives, a UGREEN DXP2800 at $389.99 takes about 43 months to pay for itself once its own electricity is counted, and a DH2300 at $239.99 takes about 24 months. Every $100 spent on drives adds about 11 months.
standout_why: The results ChatGPT cited are about features and how to set things up. Apple Support 108771 covers backup methods, 108782 covers iCloud Photos, and the iPhone guide covers backing up. Synology's blog post and its iOS Knowledge Center page explain how the Photos app backs up. None of them gives the iCloud+ 2 TB price, a NAS price, power draw or electricity cost, so none works out how long a NAS takes to pay for itself. ChatGPT's own answer suggests 2× 4 TB or 8 TB drives but never compares the cost with the $9.99 plan.
decides: This supports keeping a small iCloud plan alongside a NAS, but on cost alone the case is weak. Enclosure plus electricity plus drives takes about 3.5 to 5 years to beat iCloud+ 2 TB. That is longer than the 2-year UGREEN warranty and longer than Synology's 3-year warranty. Of the NAS boxes, the DH2300 at $239.99 pays back fastest. Buying the DXP2800 or DS225+ only pays off if the family needs more than 2 TB, where the alternative is iCloud's 6 TB plan at $29.99 a month, $359.88 a year, or if they want Time Machine for the Mac.

findings.label: Power consumption, maker spec
findings.note: Yearly cost: 16.98 × 8.76 = 148.7 kWh × 0.1816 = $27.01 a year if it never sleeps; 6.08 × 8.76 = 53.3 kWh × 0.1816 = $9.67 a year if always in hibernation. Warranty is 3 years, extendable to 5. That leaves $119.88 − $27.01 = $92.87 a year of savings, or $7.74 a month, to pay off the hardware in the worst case.

unsourced: NAS hard drive prices (4 TB or 8 TB): Seagate's IronWolf page showed no US price ('no longer in stock'), WD's Red Plus page didn't render prices, the UGREEN NAS store sells no drives, and Amazon's search returned nothing. Without them, an all-in (enclosure plus drives) payback can't be given; findings instead give +11 months per $100 of drives.
Synology DS225+ live US price: Synology doesn't list it, Newegg and B&H returned 403, and Amazon's search returned nothing. So no DS225+ payback in months.
Synology BeeStation Plus 8 TB live USD price: the Synology US store and product pages showed none.

UGREEN DXP2800 and DH2300 maker power specs: UGREEN's DXP2800 spec page redirected to a 404, and the 16.38 W / 5.24 W figures came only from third-party listings in a search snippet, so OCinside's measured 7 W is used. No DH2300 power figure was found.
